provenance.author: Independent benchmark subagent within this project
provenance.source: Newly authored natural-language examples over the existing symbolic problem family
provenance.limitation: The author shares broad project context. This is a development research benchmark, not blinded external validation.

split_policy.assignment: Predetermined IDs, before any extraction model results are observed
split_policy.allowed_tuning: Prompt/schema/debug adjustments may inspect dev01-dev08 only before the initial test run.
split_policy.test_policy: Do not retune against test errors and report that revised system on the same test as held out. Record the initial test run and separately label exploratory revisions.
split_policy.gold_visibility: Do not provide gold labels, evidence spans, source routes, or test texts to the extractor prompt designer before freeze; inference receives only its current text and problem.

label_contract.complete: A unique full path is explicitly asserted and every inference is supported in the text and proof problem.
label_contract.partial: Some valid inference applications are explicitly asserted, but a complete path is absent. Recover only these steps.
label_contract.abstain: No unique admissible asserted path can be recovered under this benchmark protocol. Do not produce a detection decision.
label_contract.expected_routes: Only stages whose first route-choice iToken is explicitly asserted are listed; a lone forced completion does not count as an observed first choice.
label_contract.expected_steps: Deduplicated canonical inference applications; comparison is set-based and ignores presentation order.
label_contract.evidence: Verbatim spans support each accepted step. A span is an annotation aid, not a formal entailment proof.
label_contract.source_routes: Reference/original paths where applicable, for diagnostics only; they can differ from the edited text and must never be passed to extraction.
label_contract.diagnostic_mentioned_steps: Optional non-scoring annotation for rejected text; these are not a selected path.

cases.text: We already have p0. Combining that fact with the conditional p0 -> m0 establishes m0. Now use m0 together with m0 -> p1; the conclusion is p1.

cases.text: The two available facts are p0 and d0, so I join them into the single claim p0 & d0. That joint claim, together with (p0 & d0) -> p1, establishes p1.

evidence.quote: The two available facts are p0 and d0, so I join them into the single claim p0 & d0.

cases.text: Starting from p0, I apply p0 -> m0 and obtain m0. I then apply m0 -> p1 to m0 and obtain p1. At the next stage p1 and d1 both hold, which establishes p1 & d1. Finally, (p1 & d1) -> p2 applied to that conjunction establishes p2.

I then apply m0 -> p1 to m0 and obtain p1.
At the next stage p1 and d1 both hold, which establishes p1 & d1.
Finally, (p1 & d1) -> p2 applied to that conjunction establishes p2.

cases.reason: The second stage depends on the first stage result.

cases.text: I used the fact p0 and the implication p0 -> m0 to establish m0. I stopped there and have not supplied a derivation of p1.

cases.text: The final answer is p1. I am not providing the argument that led to it.
cases.reason: An asserted endpoint alone does not identify a reasoning path.

cases.text: The garden was quiet after the rain. This paragraph describes the weather and makes no logical argument about the supplied symbols.
cases.reason: No inference in the problem domain is expressed.

cases.text: The rule p0 -> m0 can now fire, since p0 is a fact; this settles m0. With m0 settled, the rule m0 -> p1 settles p1 in turn.

With m0 settled, the rule m0 -> p1 settles p1 in turn.

cases.text: Put d0 alongside p0: both are true, hence d0 & p0 is true. The implication (d0 & p0) -> p1 applies to that combined fact, so p1 follows.

evidence.quote: Put d0 alongside p0: both are true, hence d0 & p0 is true.
The implication (d0 & p0) -> p1 applies to that combined fact, so p1 follows.

cases.reason: Binary conjunction operand order is canonically immaterial.

cases.text: At least one of p0 and e0 holds, because we know p0. Thus I have p0 | e0. The premise (p0 | e0) -> p1 takes that established alternative to p1.

evidence.quote: At least one of p0 and e0 holds, because we know p0. Thus I have p0 | e0.
The premise (p0 | e0) -> p1 takes that established alternative to p1.

cases.text: The last move is m0 together with m0 -> p1, which yields p1. For completeness, m0 was obtained in the preceding move by applying p0 -> m0 to the known p0.

evidence.quote: For completeness, m0 was obtained in the preceding move by applying p0 -> m0 to the known p0.
The last move is m0 together with m0 -> p1, which yields p1.

Since the problem gives (p0 & d0) -> p1, this intermediate statement establishes p1.

cases.text: The initial p0 triggers p0 -> m0, establishing m0. That m0 then triggers m0 -> p1, establishing p1. Knowing p1, I may assert p1 | e1. I apply (p1 | e1) -> p2 to this disjunction and obtain p2.

Both d0 and p0 are available; combining them gives d0 & p0.
With this conjunction, the supplied implication (d0 & p0) -> p1 gives p1.
Next, p1 and the rule p1 -> m1 establish m1.
The fact m1 and the rule m1 -> p2 establish p2.

cases.text: From the available p0 I retain the weaker assertion p0 | e0. The conditional (p0 | e0) -> p1 then turns that assertion into p1. Pair the established p1 with the given d1 to obtain p1 & d1. The rule (p1 & d1) -> p2 takes this pair to p2.

cases.text:
I begin with p0 and use p0 -> m0, obtaining m0. Then m0 -> p1 applied to m0 gives p1.

Using p1 together with d1, I form p1 & d1. That conjunction satisfies the antecedent of (p1 & d1) -> p2, so p2 is established.

Because p2 is now established, p2 | e2 is established. Finally, (p2 | e2) -> p3 applied to this disjunction gives p3.

evidence.quote: I begin with p0 and use p0 -> m0, obtaining m0.
Then m0 -> p1 applied to m0 gives p1.
Using p1 together with d1, I form p1 & d1.
That conjunction satisfies the antecedent of (p1 & d1) -> p2, so p2 is established.
Because p2 is now established, p2 | e2 is established.
Finally, (p2 | e2) -> p3 applied to this disjunction gives p3.

cases.reason: All six inferences are expressed; no stage may be skipped.
